title: Classic Margherita Pizza
instructions: 1. Preheat oven to 250°C (480°F) with a pizza stone or inverted baking sheet inside. 2. Crush the San Marzano tomatoes by hand, season with salt. 3. Stretch the dough into a 30cm round on a floured surface. 4. Spread a thin layer of crushed tomatoes over the base. 5. Tear the mozzarella into pieces and distribute evenly. 6. Drizzle with olive oil. 7. Slide onto the hot stone and bake for 8-10 minutes until the crust is charred and bubbly. 8. Top with fresh basil leaves and serve immediately.
description: The quintessential Neapolitan pizza with a blistered crust, sweet tomato sauce, and creamy mozzarella. Simple ingredients elevated by high heat create a pizza that's hard to beat.

title: Spaghetti Carbonara
instructions: 1. Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil and cook spaghetti until al dente. 2. Cut guanciale into small strips and cook in a cold pan over medium heat until crispy and the fat renders out. 3. Whisk together egg yolks, whole egg, grated Pecorino, and plenty of black pepper. 4. When pasta is cooked, reserve 200ml pasta water, then drain. 5. Add hot pasta to the guanciale pan (off heat). 6. Quickly pour the egg mixture over the pasta, tossing vigorously. Add splashes of pasta water to create a creamy sauce. 7. Serve immediately with extra Pecorino and black pepper.
description: Rome's most famous pasta — silky, rich, and deeply savory. The heat of the pasta gently cooks the egg mixture into a luscious sauce without scrambling.

title: Chicken Tikka Masala
instructions: 1. Marinate chicken pieces in yogurt, half the garam masala, turmeric, and cumin for at least 30 minutes. 2. Thread chicken onto skewers and grill or broil for 12-15 minutes until charred. 3. Melt butter in a large pan, cook diced onions until golden. 4. Add minced garlic and grated ginger, cook 2 minutes. 5. Add paprika, remaining garam masala, and tinned tomatoes. Simmer 15 minutes. 6. Stir in cream and add the grilled chicken pieces. 7. Simmer 10 minutes until sauce thickens. 8. Garnish with fresh coriander and serve with basmati rice or naan.
description: Tender charred chicken pieces bathed in a rich, spiced tomato-cream sauce. This beloved dish bridges smoky tandoori flavors with a velvety, aromatic gravy.

title: Pad Thai
instructions: 1. Soak rice noodles in warm water for 20 minutes until pliable, then drain. 2. Mix tamarind paste, fish sauce, and palm sugar to make the sauce. 3. Heat oil in a wok over high heat. Stir-fry diced tofu until golden, set aside. 4. Cook prawns until pink, set aside. 5. Add minced garlic, crack in eggs, and scramble. 6. Add noodles and the tamarind sauce, toss until noodles are coated and softened. 7. Return tofu and prawns, add bean sprouts and chives, toss briefly. 8. Serve topped with crushed peanuts, lime wedges, and extra bean sprouts.
description: Thailand's iconic street noodle dish with the perfect balance of sweet, sour, salty, and umami. The wok-charred noodles with crunchy peanuts and a squeeze of lime are irresistible.

title: Classic Beef Tacos
instructions: 1. Heat oil in a skillet over medium-high heat. Cook diced onion until softened. 2. Add minced garlic, cook 1 minute. 3. Add ground beef, breaking it up, and cook until browned. 4. Stir in cumin, chili powder, and paprika. Season with salt. 5. Warm corn tortillas in a dry pan or over a gas flame. 6. Dice tomatoes and avocados, chop coriander. 7. Fill tortillas with seasoned beef and top with diced tomato, avocado, sour cream, coriander, and a squeeze of lime.
description: Simple, satisfying beef tacos with warmly spiced meat piled into charred corn tortillas. Topped with cool avocado, sour cream, and fresh lime for a perfect weeknight dinner.

title: Miso Ramen
instructions: 1. Marinate pork belly in soy sauce and mirin for 1 hour, then roast at 180°C for 45 minutes until tender. Let rest and slice thinly. 2. Soft-boil eggs for 6.5 minutes, cool in ice water, peel, and marinate in soy sauce and mirin. 3. Sauté minced garlic and grated ginger in sesame oil. 4. Add chicken stock and bring to a simmer. 5. Dissolve miso paste into the broth — do not boil after adding miso. 6. Stir in butter for richness. 7. Cook ramen noodles according to package directions. 8. Divide noodles among bowls, ladle broth over. Top with sliced pork, halved marinated eggs, sweetcorn, sliced spring onions, and nori.
description: A deeply warming bowl of ramen with rich miso broth, melt-in-your-mouth pork belly, and a perfectly jammy marinated egg. This is comfort food at its most satisfying.

title: Shakshuka
instructions: 1. Heat olive oil in a large skillet over medium heat. 2. Sauté diced onion and sliced bell peppers until softened, about 8 minutes. 3. Add minced garlic, cumin, paprika, and chili flakes, cook 1 minute. 4. Pour in tinned tomatoes, season with salt, and simmer for 10 minutes until thickened. 5. Make 6 wells in the sauce and crack an egg into each. 6. Cover and cook on low for 6-8 minutes until egg whites are set but yolks are still runny. 7. Crumble feta over the top, scatter with fresh parsley, and serve straight from the pan with crusty bread.
description: Gently poached eggs nestled in a spiced, smoky tomato and pepper sauce. This vibrant one-pan dish from North Africa is perfect for brunch or a quick supper.

title: Korean Bibimbap
instructions: 1. Cook short-grain rice and keep warm. 2. Marinate thinly sliced beef in soy sauce, sesame oil, and minced garlic for 20 minutes. 3. Blanch spinach, squeeze dry, and season with sesame oil and salt. 4. Julienne carrots and courgette, sauté each separately with a pinch of salt. 5. Sauté mushrooms until golden. 6. Stir-fry the marinated beef over high heat. 7. Fry eggs sunny-side up. 8. Arrange rice in bowls, top with each vegetable, beef, and a fried egg. 9. Serve with gochujang on the side. Mix everything together before eating.
description: A vibrant Korean rice bowl topped with an array of seasoned vegetables, savory beef, and a runny fried egg. The spicy gochujang ties all the flavors together when mixed.

title: French Onion Soup
instructions: 1. Thinly slice all the onions. Melt butter in a large heavy pot over medium heat. 2. Add onions and a pinch of salt, cook for 40-50 minutes, stirring occasionally, until deeply caramelized and golden brown. Add sugar halfway through to help caramelization. 3. Add minced garlic, cook 1 minute. 4. Deglaze with white wine, scraping up browned bits, and cook until wine evaporates. 5. Add beef stock, thyme, and bay leaf. Simmer 20 minutes. 6. Ladle soup into oven-safe bowls, top with baguette slices and grated Gruyère. 7. Broil until cheese is melted, bubbly, and golden brown. Serve immediately.
description: Deeply caramelized onions simmered into a rich, savory broth and crowned with a bubbling cap of melted Gruyère on crusty bread. This classic French soup is pure comfort.

title: Vegetable Stir-Fry with Tofu
instructions: 1. Press tofu for 15 minutes, then cut into cubes and toss with cornstarch. 2. Heat vegetable oil in a wok over high heat. Fry tofu until golden and crispy on all sides, set aside. 3. Add a splash more oil, stir-fry sliced carrots and broccoli for 2 minutes. 4. Add sliced bell pepper and snap peas, cook 2 more minutes. 5. Add minced garlic and grated ginger, cook 30 seconds. 6. Return tofu to the wok, add soy sauce and rice vinegar, toss to coat. 7. Drizzle with sesame oil and serve over steamed rice.
description: Crispy golden tofu with vibrant wok-tossed vegetables in a savory soy and ginger sauce. A quick, healthy meal that delivers big flavor in minimal time.

title: Chicken Caesar Salad
instructions: 1. Season chicken breasts with salt, pepper, and olive oil. Grill or pan-fry over medium-high heat for 6-7 minutes per side until cooked through. Rest 5 minutes, then slice. 2. Cube bread, toss with olive oil, and bake at 200°C for 8-10 minutes until golden and crunchy. 3. Make dressing: blend egg yolk, anchovy fillets, garlic, Dijon, lemon juice, and Worcestershire sauce. Slowly drizzle in olive oil while blending until emulsified. 4. Chop romaine and toss with the dressing. 5. Top with sliced chicken, croutons, and shaved Parmesan.
description: Crisp romaine lettuce coated in a creamy, tangy homemade Caesar dressing with juicy grilled chicken and crunchy croutons. A timeless salad that never disappoints.

title: Thai Green Curry
instructions: 1. Heat oil in a wok or large pan. Fry green curry paste for 2 minutes until fragrant. 2. Add the thick cream from the top of the coconut milk, stir into the paste, and cook until oil separates. 3. Add sliced chicken and cook for 5 minutes. 4. Pour in remaining coconut milk, add quartered aubergines and bamboo shoots. 5. Add torn kaffir lime leaves, fish sauce, and palm sugar. 6. Simmer for 15-20 minutes until chicken is cooked and aubergines are tender. 7. Stir in Thai basil and sliced red chili. 8. Serve over jasmine rice.
description: An aromatic, coconut-rich Thai curry with tender chicken and vegetables swimming in a vibrant green sauce. Fragrant with lemongrass, galangal, and Thai basil.

title: Classic Hummus
instructions: 1. Drain and rinse chickpeas. For extra smooth hummus, rub between your hands to remove the skins. 2. Add chickpeas to a food processor with tahini, lemon juice, garlic, cumin, and salt. 3. Blend for 3-4 minutes, scraping down sides. 4. With the processor running, slowly drizzle in ice water until the hummus is very smooth and fluffy. 5. Taste and adjust seasoning. 6. Spread on a plate, create a swirl with the back of a spoon, drizzle generously with olive oil, and dust with paprika. Serve with warm pita or vegetables.
description: Ultra-creamy, lemony hummus made silky smooth with quality tahini and a splash of ice water. This Middle Eastern staple is endlessly versatile as a dip, spread, or side.

title: Beef Bulgogi
instructions: 1. Blend soy sauce, sesame oil, brown sugar, garlic, ginger, grated pear, and half the onion into a smooth marinade. 2. Toss the thinly sliced beef in the marinade and refrigerate for at least 30 minutes (ideally 2 hours). 3. Heat a grill or cast-iron pan to very high heat. 4. Cook beef in batches without overcrowding, searing for 2-3 minutes per side until caramelized. 5. Slice the remaining onion into rings and grill alongside. 6. Garnish with sliced spring onions and sesame seeds. 7. Serve with steamed rice and lettuce leaves for wrapping.
description: Sweet, savory, and smoky Korean grilled beef marinated in a blend of soy sauce, pear, and sesame. The caramelized edges make every bite irresistible wrapped in crisp lettuce.

title: Mushroom Risotto
instructions: 1. Keep vegetable stock warm in a saucepan over low heat. 2. Sauté sliced mushrooms in olive oil over high heat until golden, season and set aside. 3. In the same pan, melt half the butter and cook diced onion until translucent. Add garlic, cook 1 minute. 4. Add arborio rice, stir for 2 minutes until edges are translucent. 5. Pour in white wine and stir until absorbed. 6. Add warm stock one ladle at a time, stirring frequently, waiting for each addition to absorb before adding the next. This takes about 18-20 minutes. 7. When rice is creamy and al dente, fold in mushrooms, remaining butter, Parmesan, and thyme leaves. 8. Rest for 2 minutes, then serve.
description: Luxuriously creamy risotto studded with golden sautéed mushrooms and finished with Parmesan and butter. The gentle stirring creates the signature velvety texture.

title: Falafel Wrap
instructions: 1. Drain the soaked chickpeas thoroughly. 2. Pulse in a food processor with parsley, coriander, onion, garlic, cumin, and ground coriander until a coarse paste forms — do not over-process. 3. Mix in baking powder and salt. Refrigerate for 30 minutes. 4. Form into small patties or balls. 5. Deep-fry in 180°C oil for 3-4 minutes until deep golden and crispy. Drain on paper towels. 6. Warm flatbreads, fill with falafel, sliced tomatoes, cucumber, pickled turnips, and drizzle generously with tahini sauce.
description: Crispy, herb-packed falafel made from soaked chickpeas for the perfect crunch. Wrapped in warm flatbread with fresh vegetables and creamy tahini for a satisfying handheld meal.

title: Japanese Chicken Katsu Curry
instructions: 1. For the curry sauce: cook diced onions in oil until very soft and golden, about 15 minutes. 2. Add diced carrots and potato, cook 5 minutes. 3. Stir in curry powder and garam masala, cook 2 minutes. 4. Add chicken stock, soy sauce, and honey. Simmer 20 minutes until vegetables are tender. 5. Blend half the sauce for a smooth consistency, stir back in. 6. For the katsu: pound chicken breasts to even thickness. Coat in flour, dip in beaten egg, then press into panko. 7. Shallow-fry in oil at 170°C for 5-6 minutes per side until golden and cooked through. 8. Slice katsu, serve over rice with curry sauce ladled alongside.
description: Crispy panko-crusted chicken cutlets served with a sweet, mellow Japanese curry sauce. The satisfying crunch against the velvety curry makes this a beloved comfort dish.

title: Guacamole
instructions: 1. Halve avocados, remove the stones, and scoop flesh into a bowl. 2. Mash with a fork to your preferred texture — chunky or smooth. 3. Finely dice the red onion, jalapeño (seeds removed for less heat), and tomato. 4. Mince the garlic and chop the coriander. 5. Fold everything into the avocado with the juice of both limes and salt. 6. Taste and adjust seasoning. 7. Serve immediately with tortilla chips or as a taco topping.
description: Fresh, vibrant guacamole with ripe avocados, zesty lime, and a kick of jalapeño. Best made just before serving when the avocados are perfectly ripe and buttery.

title: Teriyaki Salmon
instructions: 1. Mix soy sauce, mirin, honey, rice vinegar, minced garlic, and grated ginger to make the teriyaki sauce. 2. Pat salmon fillets dry and season with salt. 3. Heat a non-stick pan over medium-high heat with a little oil. 4. Sear salmon skin-side down for 4 minutes until crispy. 5. Flip and cook 2 more minutes. 6. Pour teriyaki sauce into the pan, let it bubble and reduce around the salmon for 2 minutes, spooning it over the fish. 7. Serve over steamed rice, drizzle with remaining sauce, and top with sesame seeds and sliced spring onions.
description: Perfectly seared salmon with crispy skin glazed in a sweet-savory teriyaki sauce. Quick enough for a weeknight yet elegant enough for guests.

title: Butter Chicken (Murgh Makhani)
instructions: 1. Marinate chicken in yogurt, chili powder, and salt for at least 30 minutes. 2. Grill or pan-fry marinated chicken pieces until charred, set aside. 3. Melt butter in a large pan, cook diced onion until deep golden brown. 4. Add garlic and ginger paste, cook 2 minutes. 5. Add tinned tomatoes and simmer for 15 minutes. Blend until smooth. 6. Return sauce to the pan, add garam masala, cumin, and sugar. 7. Add grilled chicken pieces and simmer 10 minutes. 8. Stir in cream and crushed fenugreek leaves. 9. Adjust seasoning and serve with naan or rice.
description: Smoky tandoori-style chicken in an incredibly rich, velvety tomato-butter sauce. The gentle sweetness and warming spices make this one of India's most beloved exports.

title: Crispy Peking Duck Pancakes
instructions: 1. Dry the duck thoroughly inside and out. Rub with salt and five-spice powder. Place uncovered in the fridge overnight to dry the skin. 2. The next day, mix honey, rice vinegar, and soy sauce. Brush over the entire duck. 3. Let air-dry for 1 hour. 4. Preheat oven to 180°C. Place duck on a rack over a roasting tin. Roast for 1.5 hours, basting with honey glaze every 30 minutes. 5. Increase to 220°C for the final 15 minutes for extra crispy skin. 6. Rest the duck 15 minutes, then shred the meat and crispy skin. 7. Steam pancakes, julienne cucumber and spring onions. 8. Serve the duck with pancakes, hoisin sauce, cucumber, and spring onions for wrapping.
description: Gloriously crispy-skinned duck shredded and wrapped in delicate pancakes with hoisin sauce, cucumber, and spring onions. A celebratory Chinese dish worth the effort.

title: Classic American Cheeseburger
instructions: 1. Divide beef into 4 portions, form into patties slightly larger than the buns (they'll shrink). Season generously with salt and pepper. 2. Heat a cast-iron skillet or grill to high heat. 3. Cook patties for 3-4 minutes per side for medium. In the last minute, add a slice of cheese on each patty and cover to melt. 4. Toast the buns in butter until golden. 5. Assemble: bottom bun, ketchup, lettuce, tomato slice, patty with cheese, pickles, onion rings, mustard, top bun. 6. Serve immediately with fries.
description: A no-nonsense American cheeseburger with a juicy, well-seasoned beef patty and melted cheese on a buttery toasted bun. Simple, satisfying, and endlessly craveable.

title: Palak Paneer
instructions: 1. Blanch spinach in boiling water for 2 minutes, then transfer to ice water. Drain and blend into a smooth purée. 2. Cut paneer into cubes and lightly fry in oil until golden on each side. Set aside. 3. Heat butter in a pan, add cumin seeds and let them splutter. 4. Add diced onion, cook until softened. Add garlic, ginger, and green chili paste, cook 2 minutes. 5. Add the spinach purée and garam masala, simmer for 10 minutes. 6. Add paneer cubes and stir gently. 7. Finish with cream, adjust salt, and serve with naan or rice.
description: Golden paneer cubes nestled in a vibrant, velvety spinach sauce seasoned with aromatic spices. This North Indian classic is rich in flavor and iron.

title: Crème Brûlée
instructions: 1. Preheat oven to 150°C (300°F). 2. Split the vanilla bean and scrape out the seeds. Heat cream with the vanilla seeds and pod until just simmering. Remove from heat and let steep 10 minutes. 3. Whisk egg yolks and caster sugar until pale and thick. 4. Slowly pour the warm cream into the yolks, whisking constantly. Strain through a fine sieve. 5. Divide among 4 ramekins. Place in a deep baking dish and pour hot water halfway up the sides. 6. Bake for 40-45 minutes until set but still jiggly in the center. 7. Chill for at least 4 hours. 8. Sprinkle demerara sugar on top and caramelize with a kitchen torch until golden and crackly.
description: A silky vanilla custard beneath a thin shell of crackling caramelized sugar. The satisfying crack of the torch-fired top reveals the cool, creamy perfection beneath.

title: Chicken Fajitas
instructions: 1. Slice chicken into strips. Toss with cumin, smoked paprika, chili powder, minced garlic, lime juice, and olive oil. Marinate 15 minutes. 2. Slice bell peppers and onion into strips. 3. Heat a large skillet or griddle to high heat. Cook chicken strips for 5-6 minutes until charred and cooked through. Set aside. 4. In the same pan, cook peppers and onions for 4-5 minutes until slightly charred but still crisp. 5. Warm tortillas in a dry pan. 6. Serve the sizzling chicken and peppers with warm tortillas, sour cream, coriander, and lime wedges.
description: Sizzling strips of spiced chicken with charred peppers and onions served on warm tortillas. The smoky, citrusy flavors and interactive serving style make this a crowd favorite.

title: Vegetable Pad See Ew
instructions: 1. If using dried rice noodles, soak in warm water until pliable, then drain. 2. Heat oil in a wok over the highest heat until smoking. 3. Add minced garlic and stir for 10 seconds. 4. Add noodles and spread flat against the wok — let them char without stirring for 1 minute. 5. Flip and add dark soy sauce, light soy sauce, and sugar. Toss to coat. 6. Push noodles aside, add broccoli with a splash of water, and cook 2 minutes until bright green and tender-crisp. 7. Toss everything together with vegetarian oyster sauce and white pepper. 8. Serve immediately, letting the smoky wok flavor (wok hei) shine.
description: Chewy wide rice noodles charred in a screaming hot wok with dark soy sauce and Chinese broccoli. The smoky caramelized edges give this Thai street classic its signature flavor.

title: Lamb Tagine with Apricots
instructions: 1. Season lamb generously with salt and pepper. Heat olive oil in a tagine or heavy casserole dish. Brown lamb in batches, set aside. 2. Cook sliced onions until golden. Add garlic, ginger, cumin, ground coriander, and cinnamon. Cook 2 minutes. 3. Return lamb, add tinned tomatoes, stock, saffron, and honey. 4. Bring to a simmer, cover, and cook on low for 1.5 hours. 5. Add dried apricots and cook 30 minutes more until lamb is fall-apart tender. 6. Adjust seasoning. 7. Prepare couscous. 8. Serve the tagine over couscous, garnished with toasted almonds and fresh coriander.
description: Meltingly tender lamb slow-cooked with warm Moroccan spices, saffron, and sweet dried apricots. The complex layers of flavor develop beautifully over the long, gentle cooking.

title: Kung Pao Chicken
instructions: 1. Cut chicken into 2cm cubes, toss with 1 tbsp soy sauce, shaoxing wine, and cornstarch. Marinate 15 minutes. 2. Mix the sauce: remaining soy sauce, black vinegar, sugar, and sesame oil. 3. Heat oil in a wok over high heat. Add dried chilies and Sichuan peppercorns, fry for 30 seconds until fragrant and darkened. 4. Add chicken and stir-fry until golden, about 5 minutes. 5. Add garlic and ginger, cook 1 minute. 6. Pour in the sauce mixture and toss until chicken is coated and sauce thickens. 7. Add peanuts and sliced spring onions, toss briefly. 8. Serve over steamed rice.
description: A fiery Sichuan classic featuring tender chicken, crunchy peanuts, and numbing Sichuan peppercorns in a sweet-sour-savory sauce. Bold, complex, and deeply addictive.

title: Caprese Salad
instructions: 1. Slice tomatoes and mozzarella into 1cm thick rounds. 2. Arrange alternating slices of tomato and mozzarella on a plate, overlapping slightly. 3. Tuck fresh basil leaves between the slices. 4. Drizzle generously with extra virgin olive oil and balsamic glaze. 5. Season with flaky sea salt and freshly cracked black pepper. 6. Serve immediately at room temperature.
description: The simplest Italian salad — ripe tomatoes, creamy buffalo mozzarella, and fragrant basil dressed with fruity olive oil. Quality ingredients are everything here.

title: Tom Yum Goong Soup

ingredients.name: chili paste in oil (nam prik pao)

instructions: 1. Peel and devein prawns, reserving shells. Simmer shells in stock for 10 minutes for extra flavor, then strain. 2. Bash lemongrass and slice into 3cm pieces. Tear kaffir lime leaves. 3. Bring the prawn stock to a boil, add lemongrass, galangal, lime leaves, and bruised chilies. 4. Add halved mushrooms and tomatoes, simmer 3 minutes. 5. Add prawns and cook 2-3 minutes until pink. 6. Remove from heat. Stir in fish sauce, lime juice, and chili paste. 7. Taste — it should be intensely sour, salty, and spicy. Adjust. 8. Serve in bowls garnished with fresh coriander.
description: Thailand's iconic hot-and-sour soup packed with aromatics, plump prawns, and a broth that electrifies the senses. The balance of sour lime, fiery chili, and fragrant herbs is unmatched.

title: Pulled Pork Sandwich
instructions: 1. Mix brown sugar, smoked paprika, garlic powder, onion powder, cumin, chili powder, pepper, and salt into a dry rub. 2. Coat pork shoulder thoroughly, wrap tightly, and refrigerate overnight. 3. Preheat oven to 130°C (265°F). Place pork in a roasting tin, add apple cider vinegar and 200ml water. 4. Cover tightly with foil and cook for 5 hours until the internal temperature reaches 95°C and the meat pulls apart easily. 5. Let rest 30 minutes, then shred with two forks, discarding excess fat. 6. Toss shredded pork with BBQ sauce. 7. Pile onto toasted brioche buns with coleslaw.
description: Fall-apart tender pork shoulder, slow-roasted for hours with a smoky-sweet spice rub, then shredded and drenched in BBQ sauce. Piled high on a bun with creamy coleslaw.

title: Spanakopita (Greek Spinach Pie)
instructions: 1. Wilt spinach in batches in a large pan, squeeze out as much water as possible, and chop roughly. 2. Sauté diced onion in olive oil until soft. Mix with spinach, crumbled feta, ricotta, beaten eggs, chopped dill, sliced spring onions, nutmeg, salt, and pepper. 3. Brush a large baking dish with melted butter. Layer 6 sheets of filo, brushing each generously with butter. 4. Spread the spinach filling evenly. 5. Layer the remaining 6 filo sheets on top, again brushing each with butter. 6. Score the top into squares with a sharp knife. 7. Bake at 180°C for 35-40 minutes until deep golden and crispy. 8. Let cool 10 minutes before cutting.
description: Layers of shattering golden filo pastry encasing a savory filling of spinach, feta, and fresh dill. This Greek classic is perfect as a main course or cut into smaller pieces for appetizers.

title: Penne Arrabbiata
instructions: 1. Cook penne in heavily salted boiling water until al dente. 2. Meanwhile, heat olive oil in a large pan over medium heat. Add sliced garlic and chili flakes, cook gently for 2 minutes until garlic is golden — do not burn. 3. Add tinned tomatoes, crush them in the pan, and season with salt. 4. Simmer for 12-15 minutes until the sauce thickens. 5. Drain pasta, reserving a cup of pasta water. 6. Toss the pasta into the sauce with a splash of pasta water, stirring vigorously until the sauce clings to the penne. 7. Finish with a drizzle of olive oil and chopped parsley.
description: A fiery Roman pasta with a punchy tomato sauce spiked with garlic and chili. Just a handful of ingredients yield a bold, satisfying dish that comes together in minutes.

title: Vietnamese Pho
instructions: 1. Blanch beef bones in boiling water for 10 minutes, drain and rinse. 2. Char onion and ginger under a broiler or over a flame until blackened. 3. Toast star anise, cinnamon, cloves, and coriander seeds in a dry pan until fragrant. 4. Place bones, charred onion, ginger, and toasted spices in a large pot. Cover with 3L of water. 5. Bring to a boil, reduce to a bare simmer, and cook for 2.5-3 hours, skimming impurities. Add brisket after 1 hour. 6. Remove brisket when tender, let cool, and slice thinly. 7. Strain the broth, season with fish sauce and rock sugar. 8. Cook rice noodles. 9. Assemble bowls: noodles, sliced brisket, ladle over hot broth. 10. Serve with bean sprouts, Thai basil, lime wedges, hoisin, and sriracha.
description: A deeply aromatic Vietnamese beef noodle soup with clear, star anise-scented broth ladled over silky rice noodles and tender brisket. The tableside herbs and condiments make each bowl personal.

title: Eggs Benedict
instructions: 1. Make hollandaise: melt butter. Whisk egg yolks and lemon juice in a heatproof bowl over barely simmering water until thick and pale. Very slowly drizzle in melted butter while whisking constantly. Season with salt and cayenne. Keep warm. 2. Poach eggs: bring a pan of water to a gentle simmer, add white vinegar. Create a whirlpool and gently slide eggs in one at a time. Cook 3-4 minutes for runny yolks. Remove with a slotted spoon. 3. Toast and butter the English muffins. 4. Warm the ham in a pan. 5. Assemble: muffin half, ham, poached egg, generous spoonful of hollandaise. 6. Garnish with chives and a crack of black pepper.
description: The ultimate brunch dish — perfectly poached eggs with silky hollandaise sauce draped over ham and a toasted English muffin. Mastering the hollandaise is the key to breakfast elegance.

title: Chocolate Lava Cake
instructions: 1. Preheat oven to 220°C (425°F). Butter 4 ramekins and dust with cocoa powder. 2. Melt chocolate and butter together in a heatproof bowl over simmering water, stirring until smooth. Let cool slightly. 3. Whisk eggs and sugar until thick and pale, about 3 minutes. 4. Fold the chocolate mixture into the egg mixture, then fold in flour, vanilla, and salt. 5. Divide batter among prepared ramekins. 6. Bake for exactly 12-14 minutes — the edges should be set but the center should jiggle. 7. Let sit for 1 minute, run a knife around the edge, and invert onto plates. 8. Serve immediately — the molten center waits for no one. Pair with vanilla ice cream.
description: A decadent individual chocolate cake with a firm exterior hiding a gloriously molten, flowing chocolate center. Timing is critical — the lava center is the whole point.

title: Dan Dan Noodles
instructions: 1. Mix the sauce in each serving bowl: sesame paste, soy sauce, chili oil, rice vinegar, Sichuan peppercorn powder, and sugar. Stir until smooth. 2. Cook noodles in boiling water according to package instructions. Reserve some cooking water. 3. Stir-fry pork mince in a dry wok over high heat until crispy and browned. Add preserved mustard greens and minced garlic, cook 2 minutes. 4. Add a ladle of noodle cooking water to each sauce bowl and stir to loosen. 5. Drain noodles and divide between the bowls, tossing to coat in sauce. 6. Top with the crispy pork, crushed peanuts, and sliced spring onions.
description: Sichuan street food at its finest — springy noodles coated in a rich, nutty, fiery sauce topped with savory crispy pork. The numbing tingle of Sichuan pepper ties it all together.

title: Greek Salad
instructions: 1. Cut tomatoes into wedges and cucumber into half-moons. 2. Thinly slice red onion into rings and bell pepper into strips. 3. Combine vegetables in a large bowl with olives. 4. Place a whole block of feta on top (traditional style) or crumble it over. 5. Drizzle generously with extra virgin olive oil and red wine vinegar. 6. Sprinkle with dried oregano and salt. 7. Serve immediately without tossing — let diners break up the feta themselves.
description: A rustic, vibrant salad of chunky tomatoes, cucumber, olives, and a generous slab of creamy feta. Drenched in olive oil and oregano, it captures the essence of Greek summer eating.

title: Vegan Black Bean Burritos
instructions: 1. Drain and rinse black beans. Heat in a pan with cumin, smoked paprika, minced garlic, and a splash of water. Mash roughly, leaving some beans whole. 2. Season cooked rice with lime juice and chopped coriander. 3. Dice the avocado and finely chop the red onion. 4. Warm tortillas in a dry pan. 5. Layer rice, black beans, sweetcorn, avocado, onion, and hot sauce down the center of each tortilla. 6. Fold in the sides, then roll tightly from the bottom. 7. Optional: toast the burrito seam-side down in a pan for a crispy exterior. Serve with extra lime wedges.
description: Hearty, satisfying burritos stuffed with smoky black beans, cilantro-lime rice, and creamy avocado. Proof that plant-based meals can be just as filling and flavorful.

title: Chicken Gyoza
instructions: 1. Salt shredded cabbage, let sit 10 minutes, then squeeze out all excess water. 2. Mix cabbage with chicken mince, minced garlic, grated ginger, sliced spring onions, 1 tbsp soy sauce, and sesame oil. 3. Place a teaspoon of filling in the center of each wrapper. Wet the edges, fold in half, and pleat one side to seal. 4. Heat vegetable oil in a non-stick frying pan over medium-high. Place gyoza flat-side down in rows. 5. Fry for 2 minutes until bottoms are golden. 6. Add 80ml water, cover, and steam for 5 minutes until water evaporates. 7. Remove lid and fry 1 more minute for extra crispness. 8. Serve with dipping sauce: remaining soy sauce, rice vinegar, and chili oil.
description: Delicate dumplings with a juicy chicken and cabbage filling, pan-fried to create a gorgeous crispy bottom while the tops stay tender. The dipping sauce is an essential accompaniment.

title: Ratatouille
instructions: 1. Dice all vegetables into roughly 2cm cubes. 2. Heat olive oil in a large, heavy-bottomed pot. Sauté onion until translucent. 3. Add garlic, cook 1 minute. Stir in tomato paste. 4. Add tinned tomatoes and thyme, simmer 10 minutes to create a base sauce. 5. Layer in the aubergine, peppers, and courgette. Season well. 6. Cover and cook on low heat for 40 minutes, stirring gently halfway through. 7. The vegetables should be tender but not mushy and the flavors melded. 8. Adjust seasoning, tear fresh basil over the top, and serve warm or at room temperature with crusty bread.
description: A Provençal celebration of summer vegetables, gently stewed until each piece is meltingly tender and the flavors have melded together. Beautiful, healthy, and deeply satisfying.

title: Korean Kimchi Jjigae
instructions: 1. Cut pork belly into bite-sized pieces. Roughly chop the kimchi, reserving the juice. 2. In a pot, sauté pork belly until the fat renders. 3. Add kimchi and stir-fry for 3 minutes until slightly caramelized. 4. Add sliced onion, minced garlic, gochugaru, and kimchi juice. 5. Pour in water or anchovy stock, bring to a boil. 6. Reduce heat and simmer for 15 minutes. 7. Cut tofu into thick slabs and gently add to the stew. 8. Simmer 5 more minutes. Add soy sauce and sesame oil. 9. Garnish with sliced spring onion and serve bubbling hot with steamed rice.
description: A fiery, deeply savory Korean stew made with well-fermented kimchi and tender pork belly. The funky, sour depth of aged kimchi is the soul of this comfort classic.

title: Lemon Herb Roast Chicken
instructions: 1. Preheat oven to 220°C (425°F). Pat the chicken completely dry. 2. Season generously inside and out with salt and pepper. 3. Stuff the cavity with halved lemons, half the garlic head, and thyme sprigs. 4. Rub the outside with olive oil and scatter rosemary on top. 5. Place on a bed of quartered onion, carrots, and remaining garlic in a roasting tin. 6. Roast for 20 minutes at high heat, then reduce to 190°C for 50-60 minutes until the juices run clear and skin is deeply golden. 7. Rest for 15 minutes before carving. 8. Serve with the roasted vegetables and pan juices spooned over.
description: A beautifully golden roast chicken perfumed with lemon, garlic, and fresh herbs. The high-heat start crisps the skin while the gentle finish keeps the meat juicy and succulent.

title: Prawn Tempura
instructions: 1. Peel prawns leaving tails on, devein, and make small cuts on the underside to prevent curling. 2. Mix dipping sauce: combine dashi, soy sauce, and mirin. Warm gently. 3. Heat oil to 180°C. 4. Make batter just before frying: loosely mix flour, cornstarch, beaten cold egg, and ice-cold sparkling water. It should be lumpy — do not overmix. 5. Dust prawns lightly in flour, dip in batter, and carefully lower into hot oil. 6. Fry for 2-3 minutes until light golden and crispy. Drain on a wire rack. 7. Serve immediately with dipping sauce, grated daikon, and ginger on the side.
description: Shatteringly light and crispy battered prawns — the secret is ice-cold batter and not overmixing. Served with a warm dashi dipping sauce for a refined Japanese appetizer.

title: Cauliflower and Chickpea Curry
instructions: 1. Cut cauliflower into small florets. 2. Heat oil in a large pan, cook diced onion until softened. 3. Add minced garlic and grated ginger, cook 1 minute. 4. Add turmeric, cumin, and garam masala, stirring for 30 seconds until fragrant. 5. Add tinned tomatoes and cook for 5 minutes. 6. Pour in coconut milk, add cauliflower and drained chickpeas. 7. Simmer for 15-20 minutes until cauliflower is tender. 8. Season with salt, garnish with fresh coriander, and serve over rice.
description: A creamy, aromatic coconut curry loaded with tender cauliflower and hearty chickpeas. This warming vegan dish is protein-rich and full of comforting spice.

title: Beef Bourguignon
instructions: 1. Marinate beef in red wine with sliced onion, carrot, and bouquet garni overnight in the fridge. 2. Drain beef, reserve marinade. Pat beef very dry. 3. Brown beef in batches in hot oil in a heavy casserole. Set aside. 4. Cook bacon lardons until crispy. Add diced carrots and onions, cook until softened. 5. Add garlic and tomato paste, cook 2 minutes. 6. Return beef, pour in reserved marinade and stock. Bring to a simmer. 7. Cover and cook in oven at 160°C for 2.5 hours until beef is fork-tender. 8. Meanwhile, sauté mushrooms and pearl onions in butter until golden. 9. Add mushrooms and pearl onions to the stew for the last 30 minutes. 10. Skim any fat, adjust seasoning, and serve with mashed potatoes.
description: Julia Child's beloved French stew — beef braised to melting tenderness in a rich red wine sauce with mushrooms and pearl onions. The long, slow cook develops extraordinary depth.

title: Fish Tacos with Chipotle Slaw
instructions: 1. Mix chipotle slaw: combine shredded cabbage, mayonnaise, chipotle in adobo, and juice of 1 lime. Set aside. 2. Season fish with cumin, smoked paprika, garlic powder, salt, and olive oil. 3. Pan-fry or grill fish for 3-4 minutes per side until flaky. Break into large chunks. 4. Warm tortillas over a flame or dry pan. 5. Slice avocado. 6. Assemble tacos: tortilla, fish, chipotle slaw, avocado slices, fresh coriander, and a squeeze of lime.
description: Light, flaky fish in charred corn tortillas topped with crunchy, smoky chipotle slaw and creamy avocado. These Baja-inspired tacos are fresh, bright, and perfect for summer.

title: Mapo Tofu
instructions: 1. Cut tofu into 2cm cubes and gently blanch in salted water for 2 minutes to firm up. Drain carefully. 2. Toast Sichuan peppercorns in a dry pan, then grind to a powder. 3. Heat oil in a wok, fry pork mince until browned and crispy. 4. Push pork aside, add doubanjiang and cook for 1 minute until the oil turns red. 5. Add minced garlic and ginger, cook 30 seconds. 6. Pour in chicken stock and soy sauce, bring to a simmer. 7. Gently slide in tofu cubes. Simmer 5 minutes without stirring too much. 8. Mix cornstarch with 2 tbsp water, stir in to thicken the sauce. 9. Finish with Sichuan peppercorn powder, sesame oil, and sliced spring onions. Serve over rice.
description: A Sichuan masterpiece of silky tofu swimming in a fiery, numbing chili-bean sauce with crispy pork. The contrast of soft tofu and bold, tingling spice is utterly compelling.

title: Banana Bread
instructions: 1. Preheat oven to 175°C (350°F). Butter and line a loaf tin. 2. Mash the bananas in a large bowl until mostly smooth with a few chunks. 3. Mix in melted butter, sugar, beaten egg, and vanilla. 4. Fold in flour, baking soda, cinnamon, and salt — mix until just combined, do not overmix. 5. Pour into the prepared tin. 6. Bake for 55-60 minutes until a skewer comes out clean and the top is deeply golden. 7. Cool in the tin for 10 minutes, then turn out onto a wire rack. 8. Slice and serve warm with butter, or let cool completely for a denser, more developed flavor.
description: Moist, tender banana bread with a golden crust and intense banana flavor from overripe fruit. The touch of cinnamon adds warmth to this beloved American baking staple.

title: Thai Massaman Curry
instructions: 1. Open the coconut milk tins and scoop the thick cream from the top. Heat in a large pot until it splits and oil separates. 2. Add massaman curry paste and fry for 3 minutes until fragrant and deepened in color. 3. Add beef and stir to coat in the paste. Cook 5 minutes. 4. Pour in the remaining coconut milk. Add cinnamon, cardamom, and bay leaves. 5. Bring to a simmer, cover, and cook on low for 45 minutes. 6. Add cubed potatoes and quartered onion. Cook 30 more minutes until beef and potatoes are tender. 7. Stir in tamarind paste, fish sauce, palm sugar, and half the peanuts. 8. Adjust the sweet-sour-salty balance. 9. Serve over jasmine rice topped with remaining peanuts.
description: The richest, most complex of Thai curries — tender beef slow-cooked in a coconut sauce fragrant with warm spices, peanuts, and tamarind. A beautiful fusion of Thai and Indian flavors.
